source_refs.note: Example 25.3.1 Paracetamol (TM): a main subheading of 25.3 Synthesis of Pharmaceutical Products, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 139-139.

blocks.alt: Phenol (HO on a benzene ring) followed by four short arrows labelled 'A series of steps' leading to paracetamol, HO on a benzene ring with N(H)-C(=O)-CH3 at the opposite position.
blocks.caption: Direct synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139).

blocks.text: It can be seen that direct synthesis of paracetamol requires a series of steps. This series of steps can be decoded by its retrosynthesis as follows,
The first step is the disconnection of paracetamol from C—N bond in amide group to get synthons.

blocks.alt: Paracetamol with a wavy slash on the amide C-N bond, a Disconnection arrow, then HO-C6H4-NH with a negative charge on N, synthon (A), plus the acylium ion +C(=O)CH3, synthon (B).
blocks.caption: Paracetamol, Step I: disconnection (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 139).

blocks.text: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., 4-aminophenol and acyl chloride molecule.

blocks.alt: Synthon (A) is equivalent to 4-aminophenol (SE); synthon (B) is equivalent to acyl chloride (SE).
blocks.caption: Paracetamol, Step II: synthetic equivalents (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: The bond is broken at the position indicated because the synthetic equivalents of the resulting synthons are well known to react through a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction.
FGI has been done because it is easy to prepare p-nitrophenol and it can then be reduced to p-aminophenol.

blocks.alt: 4-Aminophenol, a reaction arrow labelled FGI, and 4-nitrophenol.
blocks.caption: Paracetamol, Step III: functional group interconversion (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: Then disconnection of 4-aminophenol was done from C—N bond, which created synthons of 4-hyrodxy aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and nitronium (NO₂⁺) cation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Step IV disconnects 4-nitrophenol (the molecule drawn in the scheme), not 4-aminophenol. The 4-hydroxy aryl anion is HO–C₆H₄⁻, not C₆H₅⁻ as printed.

blocks.alt: 4-Nitrophenol with a wavy slash on the C-NO2 bond, a Disconnection arrow, then HO-C6H4 with a negative charge, synthon (A), plus NO2+, synthon (B).
blocks.caption: Paracetamol, Step IV: disconnection (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and nitric acid molecule.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The synthetic equivalents in Step V are phenol (for the 4-hydroxy aryl anion) and nitric acid, as the scheme shows; the text prints “benzene”.

blocks.alt: Synthon (A) is equivalent to phenol (SE); synthon (B) is equivalent to nitric acid, HO-NO2 (SE).
blocks.caption: Paracetamol, Step V: synthetic equivalents (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).

blocks.text: Paracetamol will then be synthesized according to the following scheme.

blocks.alt: Phenol, labelled phenol (SM), with HNO3 over and H2SO4 under the arrow gives 4-nitrophenol; Sn + HCl gives 4-aminophenol; a downward arrow labelled CH3COCl gives paracetamol, labelled Paracetamol (TM).
blocks.caption: Synthesis of paracetamol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 140).
